newsitem.title: FINLAND: LIPPONEN SAYS LABOUR MKT EMU VIEW GOOD FOR ECONOMY.
newsitem.headline: LIPPONEN SAYS LABOUR MKT EMU VIEW GOOD FOR ECONOMY.

text.p: Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Thursday that a joint resolution on EMU signed by key trade union and employer groups would increase confidence in the Finnish economy.

"Your stance will in itself increase confidence in the Finnish economy," Lipponen told central trade union and employer confederation leaders after they had submitted the resolution to him. He called the resolution "historic".
Lipponen also said the government was ready to start talks on so called buffer arrangements with the labour market organisations at a time to be specified later.

In the resolution, central unions and employer organisations reaffirmed their commitment to low inflation, and stated that the Finnish collective bargaining system could remain in place and that nominal wages need not be cut if Finland joined EMU.
Leaders of the two biggest unions said the resolution marked a step towards their approval of Finnish participation in EMU.
The unions' views are expected to influence the votes of many left-wing MPs when the EMU issue is decided early in 1998.
